text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Swapo congress, which ended on Sunday, endorsed a central committee proposal to ensure that President Sam Nujoma is allowed to serve a third term in office, and that the constitution be changed to allow for this.
- The new Swapo central committee could face credibility problems following claims that the voting procedure was a complete mess.
- The second Swapo re-elected Hendrik Witbooi as vice president of the party. Fisheries minister Hifikepunye Pohamba is the new secretary general with John Pandeni voted his deputy.

- Swakopmund residents been succeeded in organising a meeting with Rossing Uranium over the controversial Khan River dam project. The mining group says it wants to mine uranium in the Namib desert for another 25 years and has increased its mining area substantially since December 1996.
- Negotiations on a drastic restructuring of organised agriculture in Namibia is currently underway.
